summary: The appeals challenge the High Court's declaration that Jharkhand's 100% reservation policy for local residents in Scheduled Areas for Trained Graduate Teacher posts was illegal, ultra vires, and unconstitutional. The High Court quashed appointments made under Notification No. 5938 and Order No. 5939 dated 14.07.2016, which reserved district-level Class III and IV posts for local candidates in 13 Scheduled Districts for 10 years under the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution. Petitioners include both local candidates adversely affected by the quashing and non-local candidates seeking appointment. Issues include constitutional validity of Governor's powers under Fifth Schedule, scope of reservation policy, and applicability to different recruitment drives. The State also appealed contempt proceedings related to non-compliance.
legal_provisions_cited: Fifth Schedule, Constitution of India, sub-para (1) and (2), para 5 and 6
Jharkhand Government (Recruitment of Teachers and Non-Teaching Staff in Secondary Schools & their Service and Condition) Rules, 2015
final_judgment: Appeals disposed of with directions to comply with constitutional and statutory provisions, maintaining balance between regional equity and constitutional rights, while clarifying scope of Governor's power under Fifth Schedule and validity of local residency criteria.
